name: Rot18symmetric

description_json.name: Rot18Symmetric
description_json.idea: Apply a highly intuitive, symmetrical, and standard rotation to both letters and digits. Alphabetic characters are rotated by 13 positions (ROT13), preserving case. Numeric digits are rotated by 5 positions (ROT5, where 0-4 map to 5-9 and vice versa). All other characters, including spaces, punctuation, and special symbols, remain completely unchanged. This is extremely easy for language models to compute accurately because applying the cipher twice returns the original text.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the input string:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it by 13 positions: encrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 65 + 13) % 26) + 65).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it by 13 positions: encrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 97 + 13) % 26) + 97).
3. If it is a digit (0-9), shift it by 5 positions: encrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 48 + 5) % 10) + 48).
4. If it is any other character (space, punctuation, etc.), leave it unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
Because ROT13 and ROT5 are perfectly symmetrical, the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it by 13 positions: decrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 65 + 13) % 26) + 65).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it by 13 positions: decrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 97 + 13) % 26) + 97).
3. If it is a digit (0-9), shift it by 5 positions: decrypt(c) = chr(((ord(c) - 48 + 5) % 10) + 48).
4. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.
